Latin word

nūptiae

nūptiae, nūptiārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural only · Declension on Wiktionary

a wedding, the marriage ceremony and feast

In this lexicon

  • wedding

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 47: nōn sunt vērae nūptiae; Ter. Ph. 701: apparandīs nūptiīs; Traupman 405

Notes

  1. 1nūptiae: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From nūbō, nūpsī, nūptum, which Lewis & Short marks long; the participle and its derivatives keep the vowel of the verb (nūpta).

Examples

  • Quās crēdis esse hās nōn sunt vērae nūptiae.

    This wedding you think is going on is not a real one.Ter. And. 47

    In the entry for wedding

  • Spatium quidem tandem apparandīs nūptiīs, vocandī, sacrificandī dabitur paululum.

    Surely a little time will be given for getting the wedding ready, sending the invitations and offering the sacrifice.Ter. Ph. 701–702
